population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: ever 29.5% − current 18.0% = 11.5% used and off now. ≈9.0 pts of current users are on a second or later course, and ≈4.0 pts of the off-now group restarted and stopped again, so (9.0+4.0)/29.5 = 44% cycled. That fits ~35–45% one-year persistence and restart rates that rose further as generic semaglutide fell under $75. Ever-use rose 5.5 pts (24.0→29.5), all first-time starters, within the +6.4 cap. Of ~272M adults: ≈49.0M current, ≈31.3M used and off now, ≈192M never used. Age check: 18–29 9.5% × 52M = 4.9M; 30–49 20% × 89M = 17.8M; 50–64 29% × 62M = 18.0M; 65+ 12% × 69M = 8.3M; total 49.0M = 18.0%. The 65+ band rose 3.5 pts because generic semaglutide made cash use trivial for people outside Bridge criteria. About 1.2M of the 8.3M pay cash rather than through Medicare, and DEXA-advised pauses still hold the band down. The 18–29 band rose least in absolute terms. Most young-adult growth is gray-market tirzepatide and retatrutide vials and low-dose 'calm' regimens, and state age-21 floors for non-indicated prescribing (passed 2032, effective 2033) will cut into the latter. Income: the bottom third rose 10.3→14.5% through $39–69 generic cash fills, Medicaid generic substitution and ≈3.4M imported or counterfeit users (counted here, under-measured). Top and middle rose less in level, but the top's spending per user went up (monthly MariTide, DEXA, coaching). About 31M off-now adults include ≈6M who lost coverage under gating since 2029, ≈4M on DEXA-advised or EPI-workup pauses, and people who stopped over side effects or by conviction. Never-users are disproportionately rural, uninsured, under 30, or principled refusers. Pediatric: ~0.6% of under-18s (≈440k), mostly adolescents on generic semaglutide. Adolescent bone-accrual interim results are still unreported. ≈4.5M adults have ≥5 years of continuous use, the population in which the new pancreatic signal appears.

access.public_coverage: The Medicare Bridge successor is unchanged in structure: $199/month brand rate, the $50 beneficiary copay, BMI/comorbidity criteria and the counselling visit. From Apr 2032 CMS allows generic semaglutide substitution at ≈$45 net, and the copay stays $50 because the agreement fixed it. Beneficiaries see no saving and the Treasury does. Medicare pays ≈16% of fills ≈ 7.8M users (7.1M aged 65+ plus 0.7M disabled under-65), of whom ≈2.6M use the Bridge for obesity. 2032 Bridge spend: 1.6M on brand × $199 × 12 ≈ $3.8B, plus 1.0M on generic × $45 × 12 ≈ $0.54B, ≈ $4.4B total, flat against 2030's $4.3B despite 0.8M more users. Medicaid pays ≈10% of fills ≈ 4.9M users. Most states moved to generic-first in 2032: 2.45M × $40 × 12 ≈ $1.2B, plus 2.45M brand (tirzepatide, legacy) × $199 × 12 ≈ $5.85B, ≈ $7.0B gross, down from $8.4B. The Indiana and Arkansas waivers are unchanged.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 80+ brands at $4–25/month. China: generic semaglutide plus a large unlicensed 'research peptide' export trade in tirzepatide and retatrutide vials at $15–40/month. Canada, Brazil, Mexico and Turkey have generic semaglutide, and generic oral semaglutide is sold in most markets outside the US and EU. Generic liraglutide is everywhere.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Generic collapse, but only for one molecule. US generic injectable semaglutide launched Jan 2032 after Novo's patent settlements with Viatris, Teva, Sandoz and Dr. Reddy's, alongside a Novo authorised generic. Cash prices fell to $69 by March and to $39–55 at warehouse-club, Cost Plus-style and big-box pharmacies by Q4. Generic share of US semaglutide injection fills is ≈60% by Dec 2032. Tirzepatide is still under patent (~2036), and Lilly cut direct Zepbound to $149–199 to hold share. Oral Wegovy pill and Foundayo hold at $149–199 direct. Retatrutide list is $1,499 with $399 direct. MariTide (monthly, approved Mar 2032) lists at $1,100 with Amgen direct at $349/month, mostly clinic- or pharmacy-administered. Payer mix of ≈49.0M users: commercial 47% (23.0M), Medicare 16% (7.8M), Medicaid 10% (4.9M), cash/direct 20% (9.8M, incl. ≈2.3M on low-dose 'calm'/'quiet' regimens), imported/counterfeit 7% (3.4M) = 100%. Who pays is structurally unchanged. ≈70% of covering employers still gate (≥80% PDC, verified weigh-ins, ≥5% at 6 months), and most now make generic semaglutide the first tier. Price is no longer the barrier to the molecule. The barriers are a prescriber visit, a scan, protein and time. The gray trade shifted from fake Ozempic to cheap Chinese tirzepatide and retatrutide vials. The personal-importation gap closes for incretin peptides in Mar 2033 under PDUFA VIII.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic incl. 7.2 mg; US generic semaglutide since Jan 2032)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular agonist, weekly injectable (amycretin, approved Oct 2031 with body-composition labelling)
GLP-1 agonist + GIPR antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide, approved Mar 2032)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 small-molecule, daily oral (orforglipron: Foundayo; alcohol use disorder indication Sep 2031)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda and generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: alcohol use disorder: reduction in heavy drinking days (orforglipron/Foundayo, Sep 2031), the first label built on reward-modulation endpoints
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'quiet mind', 'calm' and 'focus' low-dose regimens (generic semaglutide at microdoses, low-dose Foundayo) for people without obesity; ≈2.3M users; DTC promotion banned from 2033
binge-eating and 'food noise' in normal-weight adults
gambling, compulsive shopping and scrolling craving reduction, still anecdotal but widely prescribed by telehealth
'metabolic longevity' regimens in concierge practices, now usually monthly MariTide plus DEXA
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care (restricted in four states from 2033)
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Approvals in the window followed the envelope. Amycretin was under review at the start and was approved in Oct 2031 after its 72-week DEXA data, carrying a body-composition monitoring statement. MariTide was filed Apr 2030 and approved Mar 2032, 23 months later, after FDA asked for bone and heart-rate data under the 2029 guidance. It is the 'monthly' driver; no implant exists in the US. The mood_and_motivation driver is realised through an indication FDA could approve. Lilly filed Foundayo for alcohol use disorder in Jul 2030 with SHAPS and craving endpoints, and it was approved Sep 2031 at 'reduction of heavy drinking days'. No mood, focus or 'quiet mind' indication exists. Wellness brands and some Lilly-adjacent marketing lean on the AUD label to imply one, which is a large part of why Congress banned off-label DTC promotion. Survodutide resubmission is still under review with a decision expected 2033. Novo has not refiled semaglutide for smoking cessation, and its new trial with anhedonia endpoints reads out 2033. Bimagrumab combinations remain in phase 3 and are not on the market. Following the Danish registry EPI signal, FDA asked sponsors of all filings to add fecal elastase sub-studies. Incretin market ≈$108B in 2032, down from $118B: US semaglutide revenue roughly halved, while tirzepatide, retatrutide and MariTide grew. Generic makers and bone-agent makers are the new winners.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the commonest class effect and the leading cause of voluntary discontinuation. Gray-market vial concentration errors produce severe-vomiting ED presentations. MariTide's monthly dosing front-loads nausea in the first days after each dose.
Elevated with rapid loss; retatrutide and gray-market retatrutide cases rising.
Still no causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Reporting is confounded by counterfeit and mis-dosed vials and is now re-examined alongside the exocrine-insufficiency signal.
Population-level problem in users over 50 who don't train. It is concentrated among cash generic users with no body-composition monitoring, who now make up most new 65+ growth.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 2028 class label and 2029 joint guidance retained. Amycretin and MariTide labels carry body-composition monitoring statements. No statute.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈3.5M users aged 65+ have been on for over 2 years, so ~0.6%/yr baseline hip-fracture rate × 0.35 excess × 3.5M ≈ 7,400 excess hip fractures a year, against ~300,000 total. The 50–64 cycling-women signal (~1.2×) has been replicated once. DEXA waits eased to 3–6 weeks in most regions as mobile and retail scanners expanded, but scans are mostly reached through employer, MA or concierge plans.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelling and the 2029 guidance retained. FDA bone endpoints required in all obesity filings. The DOJ civil matter against Novo was settled in 2031 with no admission.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings mention.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association in updated reviews, including the Foundayo AUD programme.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('the grey', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Final retatrutide postmarketing SHAPS data (2031) confirm dose dependence: ~11% of top-dose users cross the clinically meaningful threshold versus ~5% of comparators. The Foundayo AUD trials showed small SHAPS increases at the top dose, which are labelled. There is still no systematic measurement in the ≈2.3M low-dose 'quiet' users. Reports of a slow 'thaw' lasting weeks after stopping are common. Monthly MariTide users report that a holiday takes 6–8 weeks to feel.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Status moved from emerging to established on the basis of the retatrutide data. SHAPS findings are in the Foundayo label. FTC actions continue. PDUFA VIII (Sep 2032) bans DTC promotion of incretins for non-labelled uses from Mar 2033.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Substantial within a year. Involuntary stops under gating continue (≈6M people cut off since 2029), although generic cash at $39–55 now catches many of them, so gated stops increasingly become switches to cash rather than stops.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Seventh Circuit upheld the Indiana waiver on procedural grounds in 2031, and the disability-rights claim was remanded and remains unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Iron, B12, vitamin D, calcium and protein insufficiency is now consistently shown in high-loss and older users. Fat-soluble vitamin deficits are partly re-attributed to the exocrine-pancreas signal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance (2029, updated 2032) adds fecal elastase testing for unexplained steatorrhoea or vitamin D deficiency in long-term users. No FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~9 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About ten years of follow-up for the earliest users. Cycling looks worse for bone than continuous use; the new exocrine signal looks worse for continuous use than cycling, and no one yet knows how to weigh the two. Adolescent bone-accrual interim results are expected 2033.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements continue; pediatric studies under way.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Poison-centre exposure calls involving incretins rose another ~60% from 2030 to 2032. Counterfeit Ozempic pens largely disappeared once real generic semaglutide cost $45. The harm moved to unlabelled or mislabelled Chinese 'research' tirzepatide and retatrutide vials. The Jun 2031 Gulf Coast cluster of 10 mg vials sold as 2 mg caused ≈310 ED visits for intractable vomiting, dehydration and acute kidney injury, plus 1 death. Endotoxin and injection-site infections continue.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CDC HAN advisories (2029, 2031). Expanded import alerts. PDUFA VIII ends the personal-importation exemption for incretin peptides from Mar 2033. Still no prosecution of individual buyers.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent; usually transient; more common with gray-market overdosing.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Excess fall-related ED visits in 65+ users with >2 years' use persist after adjustment in two claims analyses, mediated largely by sarcopenia.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: In joint guidance and CMS counselling template; MA strength benefits expanding.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency (EPI) after ≥5 years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: NEW and unforeseen. A Danish national registry analysis (Nov 2031), replicated in a US integrated-system cohort (May 2032), finds incident EPI (low fecal elastase, steatorrhoea, fat-soluble vitamin deficiency) at HR ~1.6–1.8 only after ≥5 years of uninterrupted use, with no excess at 1–4 years. Absolute rates are ~0.4%/yr versus ~0.25%/yr in matched non-users. With ≈4.5M Americans at ≥5 years continuous, the excess is ≈0.15% × 4.5M ≈ 6,800 diagnoses a year. Mechanism unknown (acinar atrophy is hypothesised). Partial recovery after stopping is reported but not quantified. It may contribute to vitamin D and bone findings.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA PRAC signal procedure open. FDA Drug Safety Communication (Jun 2032) with no label change yet. FDA requests fecal elastase sub-studies in new filings. Some gated PBM plans have not changed rules that reward uninterrupted use.

food_and_beverage.state: With current use at 18%, US salty-snack and confectionery volume falls ~3% a year and full-sugar soda ~4%. Packaged-food firms keep cutting SKUs, and two mid-cap snack makers merged in 2031. 'Bone-forward' dairy, protein and fortified foods keep growing. Premium protein (grass-fed, 'DEXA-tested' meal kits) sells to the top third, while dollar-store protein shakes and fortified cereals sell to generic users.

alcohol.state: A fourth and fifth straight year of US spirits volume decline, with beer contracting faster after the Foundayo AUD label made EAP and primary-care prescribing routine. Craft distilleries are consolidating. Non-alcoholic and 'one good drink' formats hold. Tobacco and vape volume is down sharply with $45 generic semaglutide used off-label.

restaurants.state: Traffic flat to slightly down, and spend per cover down in high-uptake suburbs. Gram-priced bowls and 'half and protein' menus are standard. Buffets keep closing. 'No-gram' independents in Atlanta, Memphis and Houston still thrive, and a few fine-dining rooms in Manhattan and Los Angeles sell tiny tasting menus to MariTide clients as status.

apparel.state: Size churn continues. Fit has become a class signal: tailoring for trained shoulders and narrow waists sells at the top, while mass retail sells stretch and adjustable waists to cycling generic users. Plus-size specialists are stable.

fitness.state: Growing, and splitting. DEXA-plus-coaching chains (Phoenix's Paradise Valley and Scottsdale have one on every arterial) charge $250–400/month. Big-box $25 gyms are full of generic users, mostly without coaching. MA strength benefits expand. Mobile DEXA vans have moved to retail pharmacy parking lots.

insurance.state: Employer coverage 64%, structurally unchanged and still ~70% gated. Generic-first tiers cut GLP-1 pharmacy trend to roughly flat in 2032. Some employers now prefer monthly MariTide administered at an in-network pharmacy because it guarantees 100% PDC, at higher unit cost. Bone and now EPI workups are line items in cost models.

pharma.state: Novo's US semaglutide revenue roughly halved under generic erosion, partly offset by the authorised generic and CagriSema/amycretin. Lilly leads US value through tirzepatide, retatrutide and Foundayo's AUD label. Amgen enters with MariTide. Viatris, Teva and Sandoz report generic semaglutide as their largest launches. The incretin market is ≈$108B, US volume is up ~25%, and brand-protection technology is still a growth niche.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being thin no longer says anything, because a $45 generic made it cheap. What reads now is how the body is thin. Trained shoulders, good posture and steady weight signal monthly MariTide, DEXA and a coach. Thin and soft, the forward stoop in over-55s, or a face that has gone up and down three times signals generic cash and no scans. Visible regain reads as gated out, or a pause someone couldn't afford to manage.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Body shape reads as income. In Phoenix the contrast is local and obvious. Paradise Valley clients pay $349 for a monthly shot given in a concierge clinic, scan quarterly, and lift with a coach. In Maryvale, people inject Costco generic semaglutide with no scan, and their teenage sons inject Chinese retatrutide vials for leanness before summer. The top third's lead in uptake fell (21% vs 14.5%), but the gap in quality widened.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Meals are smaller and protein-first. Heritage defences persist, such as Sunday dinners, church potlucks and 'no-gram' rooms. Holiday hosting plans for on, off, off-by-conviction, and now 'holiday weekend' guests who skipped a dose to eat.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list on/off and increasingly the molecule: 'generic' or 'monthly' works as a class tell. 'Unmedicated' remains an identity filter. Advice columns treat 'the grey' and dose-holiday weekends as standard topics.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is medicalised, politicised and now priced. The backlash coalition (Atlanta body-sovereignty collectives, Tulsa–Dallas congregations, supplement sellers, disability advocates) lost its price argument when generics arrived and pivoted to EPI, the grey and gating. Its sharpest new line is class: that rich people get muscle and scans while poor people get a needle.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Established at top doses: ~11% of top-dose retatrutide users cross the SHAPS threshold versus ~5% of comparators, and Foundayo AUD trials show small labelled increases. Among ≈2.3M low-dose 'quiet' users there is no systematic data. In a 2032 national poll, ~38% of current users say they have skipped or lowered a dose 'to feel more like myself' in the past year, and ~1 in 5 call 'the grey' a reason they would stop.
interior_life.framing: A side effect everyone knows, with a common name, 'the grey', and a common fix, the 'holiday'. Brands still sell 'quiet' until the 2033 ad ban takes effect. Clinicians say 'reward modulation', and the Foundayo label says 'reduction in heavy drinking days'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Gated plans make drug holidays an arithmetic problem. Skipping one weekly dose in a 30-day window drops PDC to ~77%, so workers budget one skip every five or six weeks. Sales, hospitality and creative workers schedule skips before pitches and service peaks. Employers favouring monthly MariTide for adherence are discovering that monthly users can't holiday on short notice. Lifestyle-account reimbursement of 'focus' subscriptions has been dropped by most tech firms ahead of the ad ban.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Written in the grey' versus 'written on holiday' is a running critical shorthand. Nashville's unmedicated songwriter scene persists, and a Brooklyn reading series schedules nights for 'holiday week'. Demand for intense stimulus (hot sauce, loud venues, extreme sports) remains elevated among users.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists screen dose, molecule and dosing interval. Couples plan holiday weekends around anniversaries. Monthly users describe the 'six-week thaw' as incompatible with spontaneity. Fewer fights and less desire is still the common report.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The grey was the human-interest engine of the 2032 PDUFA hearings: testimony from 'quiet' subscribers who said they didn't know what they had lost. The resulting ad ban passed with bipartisan votes. No established turnout or temperament effects; consultants still test 'calm voter' messaging privately.

state.regulatory_posture: Restrictive at the margins, after a decade of permissiveness. PDUFA VIII (signed Sep 2032) carries three incretin provisions, all effective Mar 2033: it ends the personal-importation exemption for incretin peptides, bans direct-to-consumer promotion (broadcast, social, influencer, telehealth landing pages) of incretins for non-labelled uses, and requires a synchronous visit before a first telehealth incretin prescription outside labelled indications. California, New York, Illinois and Washington passed age-21 floors for non-indicated incretin prescribing, plus under-12 specialist-only rules. A commercial-speech suit by a telehealth trade group is filed in D.D.C. FDA remains slow on new filings and approved amycretin and MariTide only with body-composition data.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate and no structural change in payers. The direct portal still lists brand prices ($149–199 orals and tirzepatide, $399 retatrutide). Generic semaglutide made the portal less relevant. The Medicare Bridge successor keeps its $199 brand rate and $50 copay, with generic substitution at ≈$45.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged in form: Indiana and Arkansas waivers, BMI-linked surcharges up to 30% of premium, ~70% of covering employers gating via PBMs. New in practice: pharmacy-administered monthly dosing logs PDC automatically, and some PBMs offer employers 'administered adherence' tiers.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers to tirzepatide. Fleets add DEXA for drivers over 55. The Army allows accession for applicants off GLP-1 for 12 months with stable weight, which remains contested. The FAA added Foundayo to medical-certificate review after the AUD label.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: With domestic generic semaglutide made by Viatris, Teva, Sandoz and Dr. Reddy's, partly from Indian API, the India story turned from threat to supplier, and US–India trade talks dropped mail-order pharma as an irritant. China is now the visible problem: unlicensed tirzepatide and retatrutide 'research peptide' exports feed most of the US gray trade. The importation closure is framed as a China measure. Section 232 tariffs remain.

events.event: CDC issues a second health alert after Chinese 'research-grade' retatrutide vials labelled 2 mg but containing about 10 mg are tied to roughly 310 emergency visits for severe vomiting and kidney injury, and one death, along the Gulf Coast; poison centres say incretin calls are up 60% since 2030

FDA approves Lilly's Foundayo (filed July 2030) to reduce heavy drinking days in alcohol use disorder, the first incretin label written on craving and pleasure-scale endpoints; telehealth 'quiet mind' brands reword their pages within a week

Danish national registry study finds pancreatic exocrine insufficiency 1.6–1.8 times as common in people on semaglutide for five or more uninterrupted years, with no excess before year five; a US cohort replicates it in May 2032 and FDA issues a drug safety communication

First US generic semaglutide injections launch under Novo's patent settlements with Viatris, Teva, Sandoz and Dr. Reddy's, alongside a Novo authorised generic; warehouse-club cash prices reach $39–55 a month by autumn and Medicaid and Medicare move to generic-first

FDA approves Amgen's MariTide, a once-monthly injection, with body-composition monitoring language; concierge clinics bundle it with quarterly DEXA and coaching at $600-plus a month, and several large employers ask PBMs for pharmacy-administered 'guaranteed adherence' tiers

FDA user-fee reauthorisation is signed with incretin riders, effective March 2033: personal importation of incretin peptides ends, direct-to-consumer promotion for unapproved uses is banned, and first telehealth prescriptions outside labels need a live visit; four states add age-21 floors after hearings dominated by testimony about 'the grey'

open_tensions: Monthly MariTide and 'administered adherence' tiers end the weekly drug holiday just as the grey has become a mainstream complaint and skipping a dose is how millions manage it. Employers want guaranteed PDC, and users want a way out by Friday.

The new pancreatic signal appears only with ≥5 years of continuous use, while the bone data say cycling is worse and gated coverage still rewards never stopping. No guidance tells a 58-year-old woman whether to pause, switch or continue.

The importation closure takes effect in Mar 2033 against ≈3.4M gray-market users, most now on Chinese tirzepatide and retatrutide vials. Tirzepatide is patented to ~2036, so there is no $45 legal substitute. Enforcement without prosecuting buyers is undefined, and the ad ban faces a First Amendment challenge.

Generic semaglutide made the molecule an income-floor good. Scans, coaching, protein and the monthly drug did not get cheaper, so the gap in uptake narrows while bodies increasingly sort by class. The backlash coalition has found in that a cause it can share.
still_true: The Indiana and Arkansas Medicaid 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins; two misses end coverage for 12 months, and the disability-rights claim is still unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
Wegovy's brand list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The Medicare Bridge successor still carries the $50 beneficiary copay, unchanged BMI/comorbidity criteria and the counselling-visit requirement.
Retatrutide's list price is still $1,499 a month, with the $399 direct price.

prose.headline: The $45 Body: Generic Semaglutide Made Thin Cheap. Now Your Shoulders, Your Scan and Your Shot Schedule Say What You Earn
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2032 nearly one American adult in five is on an incretin drug, about forty-nine million people. Another thirty-one million have been on one and are off for now. The number that changed the country is forty-five. In January, generic semaglutide launched in the United States under patent settlements Novo Nordisk had signed years earlier. By autumn a month's supply cost between thirty-nine and fifty-five dollars at a warehouse club. Medicaid programs moved to it first and Medicare followed. Medicare beneficiaries still pay the fifty-dollar copay their agreement fixed, so the saving goes to the Treasury.

Who pays is structurally unchanged. Most covering employers still gate: stay adherent, step on the verified scale, lose five percent by month six. The gate matters less now, because someone who is cut off can buy the molecule for less than a phone bill. What price can no longer explain, class does. A $45 pen does not include a bone scan, a coach, protein, or the monthly injection Amgen launched in March. In Paradise Valley a concierge clinic gives MariTide once a month and books the next DEXA. Eight miles away in Maryvale people inject generic semaglutide at the kitchen table, and some of their sons inject Chinese retatrutide bought as a research chemical. Thin no longer means anything by itself. Trained shoulders mean money. A soft, stooped thinness, or a face that has come and gone three times, means the generic and nothing else.

The gray market did not die when legal product got cheap. It moved. Fake Ozempic has nearly disappeared because nobody counterfeits a forty-dollar drug. Tirzepatide is under patent for years yet, and retatrutide costs $399 direct, so unlicensed vials from China at twenty or thirty dollars fill the gap. In June 2031 vials labelled two milligrams turned out to hold ten. About three hundred people along the Gulf Coast went to emergency rooms vomiting, and one died. Poison-centre calls are up again.

In November 2031 the drugs produced their first true surprise. A Danish registry found that people on semaglutide for five or more years without a break develop exocrine pancreatic insufficiency at well above the expected rate. Before year five there is no excess. An American cohort confirmed it in May. The absolute numbers are small, a few thousand extra diagnoses a year, but the finding points the opposite way from the bone data. The bone data say on-and-off cycling is worse. The pancreas data say uninterrupted use is. Employer plans still reward people for never stopping.

Everyone now has a name for the flatness: the grey. FDA approved Lilly's oral drug for heavy drinking last year, on a label that measured pleasure and craving, and telehealth brands selling 'quiet mind' subscriptions treated it as permission. Users manage the grey themselves. They skip a dose before a wedding, a pitch, or an anniversary weekend. Workers in gated plans do the arithmetic: one skipped weekly dose in a month drops days covered below eighty percent, so they skip about once every six weeks. Monthly injection users have found that a holiday takes six weeks to feel, so they effectively cannot take one.

In September Congress acted for the first time. The FDA user-fee bill carried riders that end personal importation of incretin peptides, ban advertising them for unapproved uses, and require a live visit before a first off-label telehealth prescription. All three take effect in March. Four states set twenty-one as the minimum age for non-medical prescribing. A trade group has already sued.

Snack volumes keep slipping, spirits are in a fifth year of decline, and big-box gyms are full. From the outside nothing looks wrong.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marisol Vega wakes at 5:40 in Maryvale and checks the calendar on the fridge. Sunday is circled. Her granddaughter's quinceañera is Saturday, so this week she skips.

At the dental office in Scottsdale she cleans the teeth of a woman whose shoulders look carved. The woman mentions her monthly shot and her quarterly scan the way other people mention their gym. Marisol says nothing about the Costco pen in her own refrigerator, forty-four dollars, prescribed by a telehealth doctor she has never met. The dental office doesn't offer insurance that would cover anything better.

At lunch she eats half a burrito and saves the rest for later, out of habit.

Her son Danny texts a picture of a box with Chinese characters on it. Retatrutide, he says, for summer, twenty-eight dollars. She calls him on her break and tells him about the Houston vials. He says these come from a good seller. She asks him what a good seller means. He sends a thumbs-up.

At four the pharmacy kiosk reminds her about the DEXA van in the parking lot, which takes walk-ins Thursdays and costs $129 cash. She drives past it.
